cells.date: Śaka 24(1), Sōbhakrit, Kārttika, śu. [7], Wednesday, Sravaṇa.
cells.remarks: Only a set of photographs of the written sides of the plates has been received for examination. The inscription is full of corrupt and incorrect passages. To record the grant issued by the king from Talanapura, of the village Bhintāvați situated in Kudugu-nāḍu to a few specified Gāvuṇḍas in appreciation of their devotion in killing the king's opponents in a fight and capturing their wives and treasures.

Registers the grant of four villages in Kānhairt-Khampanaka by the king to Mahāmaṇdalika Purushōttama alias Purushai-Nāyaka of the Vaśishṭha-gōtra who made them over as agrahāra to 80 Brāhmanas on the day of Kapila-shashṭhi! in Bhādrapada of the same year. Gives some details of the king's conquests and those of his ancestors.

Records a grant by the king of the village Kōlūru in Pulināḍu-vishaya, vishayu, free from all taxes to one Keśava-genealogy and six sons of Vijayāditya and Daṇḍi in appreciation of their valour in destroying his enemies in several battles. The donee's ancestry is given.

cells.date: Śaka 1703, Kali 4882, Śubhakṛit, Uttarāyaṇa, Vasanta-ṛitu, Vaigāśi, ba. amāvāsyā, Monday, Rōhiṇī, Siddhiyōga, Chatushpāda-karaṇa.
cells.remarks: Records the gift, made by the king, of the village Kulivappāṭi-pāḍi to a certain Suppu-ayyan, son of Aṇṇan of Rāmaṇ suppa of the Bharadvāja-gōtra, Āpasambasūtra and Yajus-sākhā.

Records an order of the king to the Rāshṭrakūṭa and others inhabiting the Kaṇḍēruvāḍi-vishaya. The grant portion containing the donee's name is lost. The record below was engraved as a palimpsest over the erased portions of the plate.

cells.date: Śaka 1377 (expressed by chronogram), Yuva, Kārttika, full-moon, Monday.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Bommehāļu renamed Lakshmīpura after his mother, by the king, to the Brāhmaṇa Māchivōṭa, son of Vallabhōṭa of the Śukla-Yajuśśākhā.
Records a gift of land belonging to the suburb Baḷagāni alias Chennammāḷāpura of Beḷakāni-grāma by the queen Chennamallāmmāḷe to Basavalingadēva, disciple of His Holiness Mahādēvadēva of Uppinahalli.

cells.date: Šaka 516(?), Ānanda, Vaiśākha, Paurnamāsi, Thursday, Vyatipāta.
cells.remarks: Evidently a forgery. Records the grant of the village Nidagundi in Kisukādu—70 by the king to a certain Brāhmaṇa by name Buśskara Chauvēra-Bhatta of the Kammeya family and the Kāśyapa gōtra. The king is said to have been ruling from his capital at Raktapura on the north bank of the river Malāpahārī. The phraseology of the inscription is very incorrect. See below Part II, para 11.

cells.language: Sanskrit and Tamil in early Pallava characters.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of four villages situated on the southern bank of the Cheyyāru in Kiḷveṇbāḍu, a subdivision of Ālgaṇia-kōṭṭam, a district of the same name, also called Nayadhīramangalam after his own surname, by the king, as an agrahāra divided into shares among 108 learned Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and sūtras. The grant was made at the request of his feudatory chief Avanichandra-Yuvarāja 'the lord of Vilvalapura', and the executor (ājñapti) of the grant was his minister Nāga-Śarma āde Brahmādhirāja.

cells.king: Vīra-Kāsavēdarasa (ruling from his capital at Chandāpura).
cells.date: Šaka 1177, Rākshasa, Māgha, śu. 16, Thursday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: The king is styled Paśchimasamudrādhipati, etc. Records a sarvamānya gift by the king at the anādi-agrahāra, Mūrīru to some Brāhmaṇas.

Records the endowment of the village named Hebbuvvana Taṭṭagaru to Sarvajña-Hēmadēva, the presiding deity at Gōkarṇa, by the Kārṇāṭa-Mahāpradhāna Ichchappa-Vadeya of Gōvā, at the instance of the king, on the occasion of a solar eclipse.

Records a gift of land in the village of Siruvalige and the appropriation of its revenue for the expenses of worship and offerings and of the car festival in the temple of god Gangādharcēśvara and Sidhāpura by Biligi Sōmaśekhara-Nāyaka.

Records a gift of land in the village of Chika- Bijjahalli of the Gūti-venthe (subdivision) in Banavāsi 12000 to Mallekarjuna, son of Mallapaṇḍita, grandson of Channamallammaṇḍi and Sōmaśēkhara-Nāyaka, 'the great lord (Mahāprabhu) of Biligi'.

Records a gift of the customs duties on all articles of merchandise passing through the nādu, by the chief, the mahāmādu, dettis, etc., for the rādhāveva of god Gangādharēśvara near Hajīkāmaṭi at Siddāpura.

Only the last plate of a set, the others being lost. Records that, after purchase from the chief, made 'after purchase from the chief', a sarsamvāya endowment (of land) in the Māsūru Mosajeyakuruvu for the maintenance of the temple services of the Pārśva- Jināra-Basti of Huligureya on the advice of Chandraprabhādēva, a disciple of Vijayakīrtidēva of the Dēsi-gaṇa.

Records the royal grant of the village Nāpāṭi-vāka in Kōlōvartani (division) to two learned Brāhmaṇas, viz., Narasiṁha- Bhaṭṭa and his brother Mādhava-Bhaṭṭa of the Bāhrivṛicha-Vīda and all the Sūtras, on the occasion of Uttarāyaṇa to secure religious merit for the king and his parents. Published in the Telugu Journal, Bhāratī, Vol. XIV, Part 2, pp. 67 ff.

Records an endowment in money made by Abbaradēvi, queen of Immadi Bhairarasa, at the request of his sister, Saṅkaradēvī, for the benefit of Chandrōgra Pārśva-Tīrthankara (basti) of Bidure. The grant was made into the hands of the Sthānikas at the instance of the guru Abhinava-Paṇḍita. Out of this amount lands were purchased. Records also another endowment of 1250 varāhas.

cells.date: Śaka 1468, Viśvāvasu, Kārttika śu. 1; and Parābhava, Prathama Āshāḍha, śu. 10.
cells.remarks: Gives the ancestry of the chief for six generations. Records the gift, by the chief, of the income from certain lands in the village Kuduingabayu included in the Kudingali-grāma-rājya-pālu in the bima called Tribhuvanabhūshana in Bidure. Records also a gift by the chief of a silver cup and of money for the provision of rice-offering to god Chandraprabhādēva in the same basti in the name of Vīramamma, the wife of his uncle Timmiarasa. Refers also to a gift of money for the milk-bath of the deity in the name of Timmappa, son of Ghaṇṭōdeya.

Records an endowment of land at Maṇakāta in Michāra-māgāṇe for āhārādāna (feeding) in the basti (at Bidure) by Abbakkadēvi of the Chauda (family) for the merit of his sister Padumalādēvi containing the injunction that the chiefs of Puttige should not destroy the charity.

States that the two sections of Jaina residents living in Bettakēri and Maḍalāṅgadēri at Bidure, who were celebrating the Divāli festivals hitherto by mutual fights with sticks, slings, stones and shields, by making a vow made up their mind that as it was against the tenets of their faith and to observe the festival in future by harmless diversions of dīpārādhana and other special worship in the Chandranātha-basti, made at the intercession of their Pontiff, Samanta-

Records separately in the same plate the earlier activities of this Samantabhadra who is stated to have visited the king at Ikkēri and his local officer Chinna-bhandāra Dēvappa and secured their financial and official assistance for the renovation of the chaityāluya called Tribhuvanatilaka, dedicated to Chandranāthasvāmi at Bidure.

cells.king: Lakshmaṇarasa alias Bhairarasa of the Kāḍamba family.
cells.remarks: States that the chief conceded certain ecclesiastical rights and privileges over some part of his dominions to a disciple of Chārūkīrtti Paṇḍitāchāryya, the high pontiff of the 72 religious samāthānas of the Jainas.

Records an endowment of certain lands in the village Bennegāve in the Sōde province by the chief Immađi Arasappodeya, son of Arasappa-odeya of Sōde, to his teacher Chārukīrtti Panditadēva who bears a number of birudas like Rāya-rājayuru, etc.

Records that Barmananda and his younger brother Kuñgiya Barmiseṭti of the Karbarabaļi agreed to pay into the treasury of the basadi of Chandōgra Parśvadēva built by Chārukīrtti Panditadēva, 600 gadyānas from out of the income of lands in their enjoyment. Also records another endowment of 110 gadyānas from the Vriśchika month of the Hēvijambi year by the same brothers.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records an agreement given in the presence of Narasiṃhōdeya who was holding the madra of Maṅgalūru by Chikkārāya son of Puṭṭa-rājaiya and the disciples of Abhinava Chārūkīrtti Paṇḍitā-dēva and the several seṭṭis and others of the mercantile guild of Bidure undertak-ing not to encroach, in future, upon the

cells.place: Do
cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: (a) an endowment of 200 honṇas for offerings to the 24 Tīrthaṅkaras by Chandrakīrttidēva. This amount was advanced to a certain Vishnu-Kalimvaru (?) who mortgaged some of his lands for the amount received and agreed to pay 16 mauṇḍs of rice as interest thereon every year.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: (b) Records a similar agreement entered into with the treasury of the Pārśavanātha basti at Bidure by Śrīdhara-paḍikōdi, who after mortgaging his lands, received 2100 Virarāya-phaya and agreed to pay as interest thereon 23 muḍe of rice every year. This was to be utilised for providing offerings and worship to the bronze image of the deity in the basti set up by Lalitādēvi of Gerasoppe.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: (c) The third record is an agreement by three brothers to pay a fixed sum every year as interest for the amount borrowed by them from the basti of Pārśvanātha ont of the endowments made by Lalitādēvī.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of money to reclaim a land at Paduvakōdu in Perañjada-māgāne which had been endowed by his ancestors for worship in the basti of Chandranātha-svāmi at Mūḍabidure, by Timmanarasa alias Achela, as the land had become fallow after sometime and consequently worship in the basti had stopped.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records the mortgage of his lands for 15 years by Mañjiseṭti of Pejāra to the several seṭṭikāras of Bidure for 200 varāhas of gold received by him from the treasury of the basti of Chandōgra Pārśvadēva at the instance of (the pontiff) Abhinava-Chārukīrtti Paṇḍitadēva.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land to the Kallu-basti of Chandranātha-svāmi at Mūḍabidure by Sātabeje-Ballāla of Marōvōḍi-grāma in Keĵada-māgāne, a subdivision of Achela-sime. The land was entrusted to a lady by name Chandramati-avva Biyyāni for performing the Salākshaṇika-nōhi (festival) in the basti.

Records an endowment of land made into the hands of Lakshmīna-Bhaṭṭāraka of the Jaina Matha, by the Gauḍas and other chiefs of Puṭṭige, by Abakadēvi Chauṭaru for the maintenance of a feeding house and worship in it.

Seems to record an endowment in money for offerings to the images of Chandranātha and Ananta-Tīrthakara by two brothers (names not clear) and the son of Vēṇicu (Vēgūr) who pledged their Brahmadeya lands for the purpose, redeemable by themselves only after a period of 40 years.

Records an endowment in lands for the performance of pañchāmṛita and other offerings to the images of Vīrabhadra and Pañchaparameṣṭhi by Rāmanātha Arasaru of Kabivara-laji in the time of Madurakēdavi alias Ātamāji, the disciple of Bhaṭṭāraka-dēva of the Śāntisvara-chaityālaya of Vēgūr.

Records an endowment of land by Basavappa-Nāyaka of Keladi to the temple of Mallikārjuna of the village of Mālari Kaḍagēri in Mannināḍa-sime by Aṇemahal Viranna in clearance of a debt owed by the former to the latter.
Records an endowment of money to be derived annually from several sources, by the chief, for the performance of various services to the god Mahābhalēśvara of Gōkarṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1300, Kīlaka, ta, Mārgaśira, śu. 15, Saturday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Grant of village Pedapalkūru by the king to Ahōbala-Paṇḍita of the Hari-ta-gōtra as an agrahāra near Maṅgalagiri on the southern banks of the Kṛishṇā to be shared by him with 8 other Brāhmaṇas as vṛitti.
Records the grant by the king, of the village Dēvarāyapuram divided into shares among Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras.

cells.date: Śaka 1481, Siddhārthin, Āśvayuja, śu. 8, Sunday, Üttar-āshāṭha.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land called Kajkuliyā-grāma, in the village Gadehalli of Iliyasa-deśava village of Bhairava Bhatta, son of Kēśa[va]-Bhatta of Muruginukuli by Madhava Hēbāru, son of Vit[ta]la-Hēbāru, during the administration of and by command of Araśappodaya for performing worship in the temple of [Nara]simhadēva at Mūdabhi[dure].
Badly engraved. Seems to record an endowment to the ēkāngi-maṭha at Śriraṅgam by certain disciples of the maṭha.

cells.date: Śaka 1301, Siddhārthin, Jyeṣṭhathā, Tuesday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Records the endowment of 22 villages in Gadag-dēśa for the maintenance of worship in the two temples of Trayambakēsa and Viranārāyana at Gadag, made by the king in the presence of god Virūpāksha on the banks of the Tungabhadrā at the instance of his preceptor Kriyāśakti-guru, and the appointment of Sammanāchārya, son of Śarvāchārya and grandson of Śankhanāchārya of the Kāśyapa-gōtra, a resident of Kratupura, to supervise the worship in the temples and manage their property.

cells.date: Śaka 1301, Siddhārthin, Jyeṣṭhathā, Tuesday, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Connected with copper-plate No. 22 above States that Gadag-dēśa of 66 villages was divided by the king into three parts, one part being set apart as Rājāmśa, the second part for the worship of the two gods mentioned above and the third made into an agrahāra to be enjoyed by the scholar Sammanāchārya, the accountant of the Gadag-dēśa and other persons of various gōtras and sūtras selected by him. (Text published in J.B.B.R.A.S., Vol. XII, pp. 352 ff.)

cells.date: Śaka 1558, Āśvara, Pushya, śu. 15, lunar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Records the sarvamānya grant of the village Pennalūru alias Bhūvarāga-samudram in Naḍumaṇdalam, a sub-division of Vajidalambattu-chāvađi, in Tirumunē-pāṇdyavaṇađu by the king as an agrahāra divided into shares among scholars of various gōtras and sūtras.

Written in very faulty characters. Seems to record a grant of several plots of land in two villages Shattiyakere (Settigere) and Mādaṅgere in the division Kunđi 3000 to a sūvanīa named Kāteya by the king who was pleased with some exploits of the former.

In characters of about the 13th century A.D. The language seems to be a corrupt dialect of Mahrāṭhi with an admixture of old Kannađa. Purports to record a grant of land at Mapināga-grāma in Kunđi 3000 province to twelve gāvundas of the place by the king, on the occasion of his victorious campaign in the southern region while he was camping on the bank of the Malāpahāri river at Kōjanūr, probably in recognition of some service rendered by them.

Records the grant of the mirāśi of the Patil: to a Gauda named Lakha-Gauđ over kusabe Hujavāđ on the condition that he should populate it and disband three small settlements subsisting in the neighbourhood.
Characters are modern and may be of the 18th century A.D. Seems to record the heroism of a certain Gauḍa (name not clear) in a battle-field.
Seal with Persian writing is engraved on the right margin. The characters are of the 17th century. Seems to be some title-deed.

Records the confirmation by the king, at the request of the minister, of the grant of a village named Tāmrapurī in Vēpuṇāma-dēśa to 110 Brāhmaṇas which had been made by the minister Mahāmātya Mallisēṭṭi, the father of Cheṭṭi-ka-pāhēra, of Pāndarīka-kāhēra, for securing prosperity to the king's dominion.

cells.date: 22nd year of reign, Vibhava, Māgha, Pūrṇimā, Monday.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Dodda-vāḍa in the Navilgunda-kaṁpaṇa of the Beluva-dēśa to Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras by the king.

cells.date: Śaka 14[3]5, Āṅgiras, Makara, śu. 5, Thursday, Uttirāḍam.
cells.remarks: Records an endowment of the village Mel-Paḷaiyūr and of 400 pon in cash by the king for worship and offerings to the images of Aliyāvradagoyṇḍa-Vināyaka and Appar Tambirānār which had been set up in the Peṇi-yaṇḍarkōil built by the

cells.date: Śaka 1499, Īśvara, Uttarāyaṇa, Hē-manta-ritu, Makara, ba. Amāvāsyā, Monday, Śravaṇa.
cells.remarks: nāṭtavar of the 84 vaļanādus outside the temple of Arunādri-Iśvara near the main gōpura at the instance of Alīyāvira-dankoṇa-Tambirānār and for sacred bath and offerings during one service of the day for the god Arunādri-Iśvara and goddess Upṇāmulaiammaṇ. Further, it records an agreement among these 84 nāṭtavar to collect certain imposts among themselves on specified occasions for the maintenance of a feeding charity in the maṭha, and the appointment of a person by them to look after the management of the affairs of the maṭha. In the preamble of the inscription reference is made to the construction of the 1000 pillared maṇtapa by the king within the precincts of the temple at Tiruvanṇamalai in the place occupied by the Periyanāṭtu-maṭam after paying a compensation of 500 poṇ to the latter (Cf. No. 574 of 1902).

cells.date: Śaka 1493, Kollam 747, Prajōtpatti, Paṅguni 14, ba. 11, Monday, Śravaṇa.
cells.remarks: Records the ēnabhoga of the village Sendottyēndai in Vēigal-nāḍu, a subdivision of Mūvarasanhōṭṭai-śīrmai in two equal shares to the temple of Kailāsanātha Vēmbankālam in Tenkarai-Vēlvānāḍu and to the Saiyva-śikhāmaṇi-maṭha situated in the Tirumadaivilāgam of the temple and Pradakshāchārya at the time by Śaṅkara-Nārāyanāchārya of the matha, Kasyapa-gōtra, and of the Dakshiṇa-Gōjaktī-maṭha.
Records a grant of land in the village to four Brāhmaṇas of Nandinigrāma and one Brāhmaṇa in the village of Pasindikūru-grāma by the king in equal shares.

Records a grant of land to a certain Vīne-Krishnamāchārya by the Reḍḍi and Karanam of Kulūru for worship of the deity Ajantyāvaram-Ananta. Also refers to agreement entered into between Vīne-Krishṇamā and others on Vaiśākha, śu. 15, in the cyclic year Vikriti, but the details of the agreement are lost.

Registers grant of lands as bhaṭṭavṛitti-manya by the Reḍḍis and Karanamsof the villages Paiḍela and Arakatavēmula to Vīne-Krishṇamāchārya, the priest of the temple at Kulūru. The first few lines on this plate (lines 1 to 10) seem to be connected with the agreement entered into between Vīne-Krishnamā and others referred to in the above plate (No 36) and lines 11 to 57 to another agreement entered into by the same person with certain others on Mārgaśīrsha, śu. 12, in the cyclic year Virōdhin.

cells.date: Śaka 1414 (expressed chronogram), Paridhāvi, Vaiśākha, śu. ... paurnamiai.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Mīgenegere as an agrahāra under the new name Immaḍi-Śrī-Narasimhapuram in the Rodda-nāḍu, a subdivision of Penugonḍa-sthala, by the king, divided into 28 shares among the learned Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and sūtras.

Records the grant of the village Kōṇaki in Palli-rāshṭra by Vishnuvardhana-Mahārāja, son of Indravarama-Mahārāja, the younger brother of the ruling king, on the occasion of the lunar eclipse in the month of Kartika. The village was divided into 120 shares and allotted to several Brāhmaṇas in specified proportion. Refers to a previous donee of part of the village by name Viḍu-Śarmā of Añkūru, the ancestors of whom are stated to have been known as Ādytikāla-Varanaruchi on account of his great scholarship.

Records the conferment of the title of Vālonpu-pul and the insignia of a Hanuma-kodi (monkey-flag) with the right of collecting mantand and maṭhumal dues in the neighbouring localities by the heads of seventy-four families of the gold-smith community, on Nallaperumal Tēvan for his victory over their opponents.

Registers the grant of the village Neduri-garāya in Muṇḍarāshtra, by Yuvarāja-hārāja Vishṇugōpavarmaṇ, the son of Skandavarmaṇ, the grandson of Vīra-skandavarmaṇ, the great-grandson of Skandavarmaṇ of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra, to the three donees Doḍḍisvāmin, Kanna-svāmin and Nandisvāmin, of whom the first is given half the share, the second two-and-the third one-fourth, and the third part of the village which was converted into a Śaraṇika, rāma (asylum) and was exempted from the 18 kinds of impositions (?), the dēvabhōga lands in it being set apart... The grant was ordered to be maintained by the state officers such as the ayutakatas, niyōgikas, rājavallabhas etc. (Edited in the Telugu Journal, Bhāratī Vol. XVIII part I, pp. 699 ff.)

Records the purchase of the village Heb-bata by Nariya of that place, for which transaction Chōla-Baicha advanced the money at a specified interest and Guru-pa and Gaṅgāperraṁa stood as witnesses. The engraver of the record was Rāyēndra-chōlāchāri. In characters of about the 13th century A.D.

Registers the grant of the village Chiru-rūlu together with Mēllamūru situated on the bank of the Krishnā, as a carōmāṇa-ya-agrahāra to several Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras by the king, renaming the village Pratāpakumāra-pura, after his own name.

Registers the grant of the village Chiru-rūlu together with Mēllamūru situated on the bank of the Krishnā, as a carōmāṇa-ya-agrahāra to several Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras by the king, renaming the village Pratāpakumāra-pura, after his own name.

The set of plates is incomplete. The preserved portion which consists of the first and the last plates of the set gives the genealogy of the dynasty, as in other records of the same king, and mentions as far as Narasa of the Tuluva dynasty. The portion delineating the boundaries of the gift village mentions its name as Kāh-vaṅgapalli alias Basavāpuram.

Registers the grant of the village Yukrūmbe to the free of Vihaichētu and situated in Pējreļkkal-viśhaya by the king from his camp at Ēruvaṭṭanagara (Udayēndiram) to Mārasarman of the Vatsa-gōtra who was well versed in the Vēdas, etc., as ēkabhōga and free from all impositions.

cells.date: Śaka 1436, Āṅgirasa, Vaiśākha, sūrya-saṅkramaṇa, Krishṇapaksha, Monday.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Haralakunta alias Krishṇārayasamudram in Kōlālā-śīrmai in the Penugōṇḍa-rājya to Kaudinya-Gōriga and Āpastamba-sūtra, who belonged to the Kauṇḍinya-gōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra, who was well versed in the Vēdas, Vēdāṅgas, Śāstras and Alaṅkāras and who adorned, as mantra, the mouth of the king (ti(ru)namāni) Kēśava. The gift was made in the presence of god Vīrūpāksha on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā.

The set of plates is incomplete. The preserved portion which consists of the first and the last plates of the set gives the genealogy of the dynasty, as in other records of the same king, and mentions as far as Narasu of the Tuluva dynasty. The portion delineating the boundaries of the gift village mentions its name as Kāh-vaṅgapalli alias Basavāpuram.

Records that Pedaḍa Hobala Reddi, administering the six samājas under Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Mahā-Maṇḍalēśvara Salva Timmarasa-vāru ruling from Peṇugoṇḍa, having undertaken to go on a pilgrimage to Ahōbilaṁ to fulfil a vow made by his forefathers, was instructed by the god, in a dream, to consecrate there a samprasi at Sāṁḍilya-kshētra near Sōmaghaṭṭa, where in (the god) would appear as Madhugiri Lakshmī-Narasiṁha, and that having constructed the temple accordingly, he secured the village Kauṇirūli-sīma into Gōraṁṭa-samutu to the god and also arranged for endowments for an archaka to conduct worship of the god.

cells.date: Śaka 1698, Kali 4876, Manmatha, Dakshiṇāyana, Varsha-ṛitu, Śrāvaṇa, śu. 5, Friday, Pushya.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land by different persons for worship of God Sōmeśvara at Vana-vān included in the Kāvēripuram-sīmai in Vadatalai-nāḍu. Records a subse-quent endowment of land to the same temple in the next year, Durmukhi, by different officials. Same as C. P. No. 195 of Sewell's List.

Records a gift of land besides authorising a levy of 2 padi of paddy per family, for the upkeep of a matha and a tank, evidently at Šivagaṅga. The Sētupati chief is introduced with a number of high-sounding titles.

cells.date: Śaka 1703, Kollam 956, Plava, Āṇi 13, śu. 2, Saturday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Records the levy of a small duty on every new or old shop in the Vijayāpati-sīmai for conducting a service in the temple of Varaguṇa-Pāṇḍēśvara at Rājājarjapuram in Murattā-nāḍu included within the trading jurisdiction of Kalakkāḍu, by Tāṇappa-Kaṇḍān, the sthānattān of Piļļai, the ayam-adhikāri of the southern region (Dakshiṇa-sīmai), for the merit of Dalavāy Tirumalaiyappa Mudaliyār and others.

Records an order of the king issued from his camp at Pangundi, granting lands for con-ducting the service called Ravivarnan-sandhi instituted evidently after the name of the king in the temple of Varaguṇe-varamudaiya-Nāyaṉār and his consort Kalyāṇasundara-Nāchchiyār at Puśān-guḍi, alias Rājājanpuram in Murattā-nuḍu. Also records that this is a copy of a stone record engraved on the east side of the central shrine of the Śiva temple at Rādhāpuram (No. 356 of 1930).
Records gift of land by Kaṅgireddi Pōttu-reddi and Nañjiyaiyan, the agents of Lakshmi-kāntayyarājavaiyyas, for conducting wor-ship daily to god Kāñchī-Varadarāyap-Perumāļ.

Records grant of land in the village of Manda in Guddavādi-vishaya, by the king to Ārnkaya alias Samastabhuvanā-śraya Brahmamahārāja, son of Rāmadēva and grandson of Śivakumārabhaṭṭa of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Āpastarnba-sūtra. The land granted is stated to have been measured by the rod called Mummađi-Bhīmakōla. Published in Bhārati, Vol. XX, pt. 2, pp. 177-193.

cells.date: Śaka 1673, Prajōtpatti, Uttarayana, Magha, ba. 13, Sivarātri.
cells.remarks: Records construction of the Siva temple on the east bank of the tank at Chaturē-dimangalam alias Sivagaṅgai and the consecration of the god and goddess therein under the name of Arunachaleśvarasvāmī and Pērumālnāchchiyar and the tour-dowment of land for their worship by prince Mudduvaduganātha-Periya-udai-yartēvar. The king, among other birudas, bears the title Arasu-nilaiyitta Sasivarṇatēvar.

cells.date: Śaka 1674, Anġirasa, Arpaisi 5, Tuesday, śu. ro, 10, Vijaya-dasami, Avittam.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of a fresh deed in place of the old one said to have been lost, by members of the Kamnala community of Ravaganmangalam to the temple of Sadāśiva-Iśvara on the tank of the tank in their village agreeing to pay a small levy to meet some of the requirements of the temple.
Registers sale of the village Tagudappadi with its 14 hamlets included in the kōdai of Kumāragiri to four Brāhmaṇas for 50,000 Rājagōpāla-varāhans.

cells.king: Muttu Vijaya Raghu-nātha Periya-Udayar-tēvar of the ruler of Sivagangā-rājya.
cells.date: Śaka 1711, Kali 4890, Saumya, Paṅguṇi 15, śu. 10, Thursday, Pūśam.
cells.remarks: Records gift of the village Miñāppūr in the Sakkai tank of the Sivagangā division by Attavanai Mayāndiyai Pillai for worship in the temple of Sēmbankōlnāsvāmin at Tempu-tūr alias Ayyundavolil in the Chola country.

cells.location: CUDDAPAH DISTRICT / SIDDHAVATTAM TALUK · CUDDAPAH DISTRICT. / SIDDHAVATTAM TALUK. — Andhra Pradesh

cells.location: CUDDAPAH DISTRICT / SIDDHAVATTAM TALUK — Andhra Pradesh

cells.remarks: States that Appalreddi-Gangiređdi, Peda-Pōlređdi, Veṅgalređdi and China-Pōlređdi, sons of Kaluvāyi Buchchi-Rāmiređdi Nārāyanamma, having decided to construct a tank across the Tummalayēru at Rāchāyapalle, Ādūri Pāpiređdi, the Redđis and Sambaṭūri Rāmachandrudu and others, and the Karayams of the village obtained permission of the government (divānahvāru), constructed the tank, established an agrahāra on śu. 15 in Māgha in the year Āananda, on the occasion of a lunar eclipse, and settled in it Brahmanas of the three sects granting them 10 vrittis of land. cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK · NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT—contd. / CHEYYAR TALUK—contd. / Tiruvattiyūr—concld. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land by Uḍaiyār-Aḍigal Mittāṇḍa-Nāñchiyar, wife of Kūḍal Āḷappirandār Kāḍavarāyar as tira-nāmaṭṭukkāi for worship, offerings, etc., to the three images of the Śaiva saints (Mūvar) in the temple of Tiruvottūr.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: West wall of the Chidambarēśvara shrine in Vēdaparīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 25 kaḻañju of gold by Ārūran Ambalattāḍigal, the senior queen (Mahādēvi) of Uttama-Chōḷa, for burning a lamp in the temple.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: West and south walls of Chidambarēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Begins with the introduction Tirumanni valara, etc. Seems to record a sale of land by the assembly of Tiruvottūr, a dēvadāna-brahmadēya in Kāliyūr-nāḍu, to the temple for a flower-garden.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: North wall of the Ekāmbarēśvara shrine in Chidambarēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Seems to record an endowment for worship to the god Aṇṇāmalai-Nāyaṇār set up in the temple by Vīra-kampa-Nāyaṇār alias Vīra-Vallāḷadēvar.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: West wall of the inner gōpura, right of entrance in Ekāmbarēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: The wording of the inscription is faulty and obscure. Seems to record a unsatisfactory mortgage, by three persons, of their shares of lands in the village to the temple for the money received by them.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East wall of the gōpura of Ekāmbarēśvara, right of entrance. †
cells.remarks: Records an agreement made among the trustees, the Mahēśvaras and the accountant of the temple, in the regime of Aṇṇādāna Pōrṛuppillai, the agent of Kōṇēri Timmaya-ṇṇan-Mārāyar, to supply, out of the taxes etc. belonging to the temple, such as tiruppavittiram, poles of temple, umbrella (tīrśadudaṇḍu), rope and ornaments of the temple-car, umbrella, etc.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK · Veḷiyanallūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Boulder near a ruined Śiva temple on a hillock.
cells.king: Rājēndra Rājakēsarivarman who des-troyed ships at Śālai.
cells.remarks: Records that the temple of Brahmēśvara alias Mahādēva at Veḷiyanallūr in Kāliyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kāliyūr-kōṭṭam, was constructed by Kañjāru Pōśan Vēngadavan-Śūryadēvan who, along with his younger brother Sūrya-dēvan also, provided land for providing offerings to the deity during the midday and night service.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same boulder
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land in Śattanallūr for Kaṇṇiḍu-Kiḷān for offerings to the god at Veḷiyanallūr.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same boulder
cells.date: 27th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 125: Śaka 1477, Ānanda, Kaṇṇi, ba. 8, Tuesday =A. D. 1554, September 18, Tuesday, f.d.t. ·22. The Śaka year was current.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Tirumagalpōla, etc. Records gift of sheep by the two persons mentioned in No. 123 above for burning two perpetual lamps in the temple.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK · Sumangali — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: South wall of the central shrine in the ruined Śiva temple.
cells.remarks: States that the temple of Āḷudaiyār Torrai-Nāyaka at Tiruk-kāmakkōṭṭam-Sumangali in Kāyāṛambēḍu-nāḍu, a sub-division of Kāliyūr-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayangoṇḍaśōḷa-maṇḍalam was long time in ruins and that it was dismantled and re-constructed of stone by three persons of Vāvalūr named Orrikoṇḍān, Āḍuvaṇ Śelvan and Perumāp Agattiyāḷvān.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Slab built into the west wall of the maṇḍapa in front of Śiva temple. †
cells.remarks: In characters of about the 9th century A.D. States that Kaḍiyākaṇ, son of Oṭṭūran, the headman of Kommai, constructed the temple and that he presented lands for its upkeep.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK · NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT—contd. / CHEYYAR TALUK—contd. / Sumangali—contd. — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East wall of Śiva temple †
cells.remarks: States that the maṇḍapa in the temple of Kōvrai-Nāyaka was constructed by Sēlvai alias Vajavadaraiyan Maḍaḍai, the headman of Vāvalūr.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK · Karaṇḍai — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Base of the central shrine in the Kunthu-Tirthankara temple.
cells.remarks: Records a sale of land, mado tax-free, by three members of the assembly (ūr) as tiruviḷappuram to the Jaina temple at Karaṇḍai, hamlet of Tirukkāmakkōṭṭapuram.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same base
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Registers gift of sheep for a perpetual lamp in the temple of Arugaradēvar (Arhat) Vīrarājēndrapperum-baḷi-Ālvār by Tugilikkāṇ Arayan Uḍaiyān of Kaḷiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kāliyūr-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Wing-stone of steps leading to the Chōla maṇḍapa in front of Kunthu-Tirthankara temple. †
cells.date: 11th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 131: Śaka 1349, Plavaṅga, Kaṇṇi, ba. [12], Wednesday, Āyilyam =A. D. 1427, September 17, Wednesday; f.d.t. ·21; ·55.]
cells.remarks: Gives a list of lamps endowed by the Nāgarattār of Arumōji-dēvapuram, a nagaram in Paṇaiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Rāja-rājanrājya-kuḍu(chchi) in the course of the waking ceremony (tiruppuḷiyuchchuḍu) in the same temple of Vīrarājēndrapperumpalli at Tirupparambūr.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Second wing-stone of the same steps
cells.date: 10th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 132: Śaka 1447, Tāraṇa, Vriśchika, śu. 15, Thursday, Kārttigai =A. D. 1524, November 10, Thursday; f.d.t. ·26; f.d.n. ·07. The Śaka year was current.]
cells.remarks: Records gift of cows by a Veĵāla of Ūrrukkādu in Ūrrukkātuk-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayangoṇdaśōla-maṇdalam, for a perpetual lamp in the same temple.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Pedestal kept inside Kunthu-Tirthankara temple †
cells.date: Śaka 1482, Raudri, Vriśchika, śu. 5, Friday, Tiruvōṇam =A. D. 1560, November 22, Friday; ·36; ·37. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 133]
cells.remarks: States that only they are the Śiddhas whose mouths recite the mantras invoking certain specified sacred namés.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Another pedestal with a pair of feet in Kunthu-Tirthankara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives the name Munibhadrāsvāmin.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: West and south sides of the base of the Chōla Vardhamāna shrine in Kunthu-Tirthankara temple. †

cells.remarks: Records sale of land as paḷicchandam by the assembly (ūr) of Tirapparambūr in Tirukkāmakkōṭṭapuram situated in Kuḷiyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Kāliyūr-kōṭṭam, a district of Jayangoṇḍasōḷa-maṇḍalam, to the temple of Tirukkāṭṭampalli-Ālvār in the village.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East base of the Dharmadēvī shrine in Chōla Vardhamāna shrine. †
cells.date: Šaka 1669, Kali 4848, Prabhava (expired), Vibhava, Vaiyāśi, Jyēchtha, śu. 5, Friday, Punarvasu.
cells.remarks: Records the renovation in mortar of the gōpura of the shrine of Kuṇthunāthasvāmi Dēvārisavāmi in Munigiri by Āgasiyappa-Nayanar.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Slab built into the wall of the prākāra. Vijayanagara nea-the gōpura in Dharmadēvī shrine. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Records gift of land in Karandai as sērumānya by Vāla (Bāla) Nagēma-Nāyaka and the taḷattar (to the scholar?) Kayilāyappullavar.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: West wall of the prākāra of Dharmadēvī †
cells.remarks: Records gift of 3 sandhi-vilakkus and paddy by Aruvaṇḍai Āṇḍāl Tiruchchōpuruḍai-Uḍaiyār of Poṇṇūr for burning six twilight lamps for a jāmam (i.e.) 3 hours in the temple.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions Tirunilakaṇṭan Maḷan Pūvaṇ of Iḷai-kāḍu.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Inner wall of the gōpura, right of entrance, Pallava same temple.
cells.remarks: Three verses in praise of Pallava-kōn who fought at Taḷḷāru and imprisoned the Vaḷava (i.e.) the Chōḷa king.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall
cells.remarks: Records an agreement given by the Kāvīrkaḷ of the temple to burn, for 300 kāśu received by him, a twilight lamp before the image of Tirumēṛṛalipperumāḷ in the temple of Vīra-rājēndra-perumpaḷḷi at Tirukkāmakkōṭṭam alias Tiruppu-rambur in Iḷaikāḍu situated in Veṇkunra-kōṭṭam.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same wall, left of entrance

cells.remarks: Verses in praise of the chief mentioned in No. 140 above, who is here called Tirubuvanatt-irējakkaḷ-Tambirān, of his encounter with the Chōḷa king.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Door-jamb of the entrance in the gōpura of Dharmadēvī. †
cells.remarks: Three verses in praise of the prowess of Kōpperuñjinga.

cells.location: NORTH ARCOT DISTRICT / CHEYYAR TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Slab set up in front of Dharmadēvī shrine †
